name: Source checkout
responsibility: The port of a server (4242 for a release, 3000 for the main checkout, a hash of the path for a worktree), the address a browser opens, and the hand-off to another checkout
description: The main checkout has a .git directory; a linked worktree has a .git file and takes 10000 + sha256(root path) mod 10000. The default server URL, the --url default and the server's own port all come from here. Which checkout this process runs comes from Installation. The hand-off follows the working directory, not -C, and does not happen when the environment sets ARCHBOARD_URL: the URL already names the server, and every Codex thread sets it, so a workhorse in another archboard checkout runs the server's own source (ADR 0050). It waits for the other checkout's command, passes SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP on to it and answers with its exit status, and it refuses a checkout with no node_modules, naming the bun install to run there. A release listens on 4242, which is easy to remember and lies outside the worktree range, so a release and a checkout run side by side. The CLI connects to 127.0.0.1, and a person's browser opens archboard.localhost, which Chrome and Firefox resolve to the loopback address themselves. The addresses that the CLI and the server show a person go through browserUrl.
